checks.detail: Exact original/source-recovery/fresh-Java-recovery bindings, original private server identity, successful read-only receipt, exact closed June/July source and target, held August capture, and explicit protocol2 admission are required before the separately bounded source append.

All five original ledger tables (runs, entries, events, groups, leases) must match both the historical authority and fresh read-only receipt, including all eight operations/eighteen entries, parent links, canonical requests and recorded ACK proofs. Before/after current file-only SQLite inspections require terminal states and zero leases; each pre-write boundary repeats the full five-table equality.

Original final-serialization JUnit failure, source INSERT UNKNOWN, and unavailable original Java PID/birth remain explicit. The completed foreground executor and frozen synchronous sender lifecycle scope prove only the retained original initial-test boundary. The fresh known read-only JVM STOP is validated against its own prewritten exact PID/birth, successful executor and JUnit, then rechecked at write boundaries; it does not replace or invent the original producer identity.

Only sixteen actual August rows covering the sixteen fixed codes and all fourteen physical fields can be submitted, in one finite INSERT INTO index_monthly. The fixed CREATE_NEW claim denies any existing ACK/UNKNOWN claim replay. No target/output/formal DDL or DML is admitted; the final source must grow by exactly one physical/WAL transaction to forty-eight rows.

A durable unknown intent precedes the single HTTP attempt. Actual response bytes, HTTP status, byte count and body SHA are saved to the claim before JSON parsing or acknowledgment. Status/cap, duplicate JSON keys and exact DML OK shape/count are checked before ACK; failure stops without automatic resend.

Fresh initial source schema/frontier and full thirty-two-row fourteen-field transport, Java output schema/frontier and two-row thirty-field oracle, protected ordinary output, formal whole-source/output authority, five-table ledger and server identity are checked before intent and before send. After the append, all forty-eight source rows/bits and complete three-month coverage must match the captured formal source; protected outputs/formal/ledger identities and values stay unchanged.

The new supplement overrides the older percent/percentage-point wording: all returns are unchanged stored index_monthly.pct_chg values; spreads use those same stored units. No division/multiplication by 100, rounding or signed-zero normalization is introduced.

actual_readonly_evidence.scope: Referenced actual root-run SELECT-only evidence, not executed by this review

limitations: Static review only. No source append, Java materialization, DB query, native query, owner invocation, Gradle or tests were run by this reviewer.
The old source INSERT ACK remains UNKNOWN and the original Java JUnit remains FAILED_RECEIPT_SERIALIZATION; the missing original Java PID/birth is not reconstructed.

Fresh read-only JVM STOP refers solely to the documented read-only recovery process. Dynamic gates must continue to revalidate its identity evidence, the current service identity and all immutable proof hashes before the one admitted append.

The append prepares isolated August source data only; it does not verify a new Java output/checkpoint, admit a later task, certify formal refresh, provider universe, point-in-time history or caller cutover.
Formal June/July derived-output gaps remain diagnosed and unrepaired. Original Python numeric values are compared without scaling, rounding or tolerance.
HTTP timeout20 is a socket timeout, not a whole-operation deadline; the existing bounded PG helper and finite WAL visibility wait remain separate controls.
